theme: The writing on the wall; the den of lions
readingInstruction: Read Daniel 5:1-6:28. A king’s feast ends with a hand writing on the wall, and an elderly Daniel is thrown into a den of lions for praying. Read the two stories together as the fall of the proud and the rescue of the faithful.
settingTheScene: Chapter 5 takes place in 539 BC, the night Babylon fell to the Medes and Persians. Belshazzar, the crown prince and co-regent, holds a great feast and uses the sacred vessels from Jerusalem’s temple as drinking cups. Chapter 6 takes place under Darius the Mede, in the early years of Persian rule. Daniel is now an old man of about eighty, and his enemies set a trap using his prayer life.
observation: “Belshazzar… gave command to bring the gold and silver vessels that Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken out of the temple in Jerusalem” (5:2).
“Immediately the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall” (5:5).
“You have not humbled your heart, though you knew all this, but you have lifted up yourself against the Lord of heaven” (5:22-23).
“You have been weighed in the balances and found wanting” (5:27).
“That very night Belshazzar the Chaldean king was killed” (5:30).
“When Daniel knew that the document had been signed, he went to his house… and he got down on his knees three times a day and prayed and gave thanks before his God, as he had done previously” (6:10).
“My God sent his angel and shut the lions” mouths, and they have not harmed me, because I was found blameless before him’ (6:22).
interpretation:
Belshazzar’s feast shows the arrogance of a ruler who has learned nothing. His grandfather Nebuchadnezzar had been humbled, yet he drinks from the vessels of God’s temple and praises the gods of gold and silver. The hand appears, and the king is terrified, his knees knocking. The wise men cannot read it. The queen mother recommends Daniel. He refuses the reward and reads the sentence: God has numbered the days of your kingdom, weighed you, and divided it. The words are about weights: a mina, a shekel, and half-shekels. The reading is clear: the kingdom is over. That very night, Babylon fell.

The charge is that Belshazzar knew what had happened to Nebuchadnezzar and did not humble himself. Knowledge without humility is the greater guilt. “The God in whose hand is your breath, and whose are all your ways, you have not honored.”

Chapter 6 is a contrast. Daniel’s enemies, jealous of his rank, can find no fault in him except “in the law of his God.” They persuade the king to sign a decree that no one may pray to any god or man except the king for thirty days. Daniel, hearing it, does exactly what he had always done. He goes to his upper room, opens his windows toward Jerusalem, and prays three times a day. He does not make a show, and does not hide. He simply continues.

He is thrown to the lions. The king, who loves him, spends a sleepless night. At dawn, Daniel is alive. “My God sent his angel and shut the lions” mouths.’ The king issues a new decree: that in all his kingdom people are to tremble before the God of Daniel, “for he is the living God, enduring forever; his kingdom shall never be destroyed.”

Two kings, two responses. Belshazzar lifted himself up and fell. Daniel humbled himself in prayer and was preserved. The difference is not strength but allegiance.
connection: Jesus said, “Pray then like this: Our Father in heaven” (Matthew 6:9), and told his disciples to pray always (Luke 18:1). 1 Thessalonians 5:17 says to pray without ceasing. Hebrews 11:33 mentions those who “stopped the mouths of lions.” Acts 5:29 says we must obey God rather than men. 2 Timothy 4:17 says Paul was rescued from the lion’s mouth. Psalm 1:2 says the blessed person meditates on the law day and night. Revelation 14:8 echoes “Fallen, fallen is Babylon.”
application:
Establish a regular, consistent prayer rhythm, even if no one sees. Let it be as natural as breathing.

Examine whether you have “weighed” yourself against God’s standard. Thank God that Christ was weighed in your place.

Pray for those facing opposition because of their faith.
prayerPrompts: Ask God to keep you from lifting yourself against him.
Ask him to teach you to pray as Daniel did, with steady faithfulness.
Thank him that your breath and ways are in his hand.
